questions.question: If 14 March 2007 is Wednesday, then what will be the day of the week on 12 April 2013?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 14 March 2007 was a Wednesday.

Now, 12 April 2013 will be on:

Number of years between 2007 and 2013 = 6 years.

In 6 years, there is 2 Leap Year (2008 and 2012) and 4 are ordinary years.

Number of** Odd Days **between 14 March 2007 and 14 March 2013 = (2 × 2) + (4 × 1) = 4 + 4 = 8

8 days = 8/7 = 1 Week 1 odd day

So, On 14 March 2013 will be = Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.

There will be Thursday on 14 March 2013. 

Now, No. of days between 14 March 2013 and 12 April 2013 = 29 days. 

No. of Odd Days between 14 March 2013 and 12 April 2013 = 29/7 = 4 Weeks 1 odd day.

So, 12 April 2013 will be on = Thursday + 1 odd day = Friday.

Hence, the correct answer is ***'Option 2'.***

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an approach for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly Status Approach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monthly Status Approach **is NOT an approach for **measuring unemployment** in India.
 
• **Methods/measures for assessing unemployment:**
 
 
• **Usual status unemployment: **This method estimates the number of individuals who remained unemployed for a significant portion of the year. It typically provides the lowest estimates of unemployment.
 
• **Current weekly status: **This measure evaluates unemployment based on a single week. An individual is classified as unemployed if they were unable to work for any duration during the survey week.
 
• **Current daily status: **Under this approach, individuals who were unable to secure employment on one or more days during the survey week are considered unemployed. The daily status method is often seen as a comprehensive measure of unemployment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The unemployment rate** is calculated by dividing the number of unemployed individuals by the total labour force.
 
• The labour force comprises both employed and unemployed individuals. Individuals who are neither employed nor actively seeking employment, such as students and those engaged in unpaid domestic work, are categorized as being out of the labour force.
 
• According to the International Labour Organisation (ILO), unemployment is defined as being without a job, being available to work, and actively searching for employment.

questions.question: In which of the following regions in India are there high-grade iron ore deposit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **High-grade iron ore **deposits are primarily found in **Northern Odisha in India**.
 
• Northern Odisha in India is renowned for its abundant reserves of high-grade iron ore deposits.
 
• These deposits are concentrated in regions such as Keonjhar, Sundargarh, and Mayurbhanj districts.
 
• The iron ore found in this area typically exhibits high iron content and relatively low impurities, making it suitable for various industrial applications, including steel production.
 
• The presence of these valuable deposits has contributed significantly to the economic development of the region and has made Odisha one of the leading iron ore producing states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron ore** is a mineral substance essential for producing metallic iron through heating processes, serving as the primary source of iron for the global steel and iron industries.
 
• It typically comprises iron oxides and can exhibit various colors such as dark gray, bright yellow, deep purple, or rusty red. Iron ore exists in several forms, including magnetite, hematite, goethite, limonite, or siderite, with each form varying in composition and properties.
 
• Most iron ore deposits are found within sedimentary rocks known as banded iron formations (BIFs), characterized by alternating layers of iron-rich minerals and fine-grained silica rock called chert.
 
• These formations represent significant reservoirs of iron ore globally and are crucial for sustaining the production of iron and steel worldwide.

questions.question: The deficiency of Vitamin A causes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**night blindness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin A causes **night blindness**.
 
• **Vitamin A deficiency** can stem from insufficient dietary intake, issues with fat absorption, or liver-related disorders.
 
• This deficiency can compromise immune function and the production of blood cells, leading to symptoms such as skin rashes and characteristic eye problems like xerophthalmia and night blindness.
 
• Diagnosis often relies on identifying these ocular manifestations alongside low levels of vitamin A in the body.
 
• Treatment typically involves oral supplementation of vitamin A, although in severe cases or when malabsorption is a factor, administration via injection may be necessary.
 
• Foods rich in preformed vitamin A include fish liver oils, liver, egg yolks, butter, and dairy products fortified with vitamin A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Beriberi **is a condition resulting from a deficiency of thiamine, also known as vitamin B1. The term "beriberi" originates from a Sinhalese word meaning "extreme weakness".
 
• **Scurvy** is a disorder caused by a significant deficiency of vitamin C in the diet. It is characterized by severe symptoms of vitamin C deficiency.
 
• **Rickets** is a condition characterized by the softening and weakening of bones in children, typically due to prolonged and severe deficiency of vitamin D.

questions.question: Krishnadeva Raya, the most famous ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuluva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishnadeva Raya (1471 - 1529)** belonged to the **Tuluva dynasty** and served as its third ruler, reigning from 1509 to 1529.
 
• Under his leadership, the Vijayanagara Empire, which encompassed four prominent dynasties - Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu - flourished.
 
• Krishnadeva Raya's literary work, 'Amuktamalyada', provides insights into his profound sense of justice and his dedication to the well-being of his subjects.
 
• He is revered as one of the most illustrious monarchs in Indian history.
 
• His reign saw remarkable military successes, as he asserted his dominance by triumphing over formidable adversaries such as the Sultans of Bijapur, Golconda, the Bahmani Sultanate, and the Gajapatis of Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Tuluva Dynasty,** the third ruling lineage of the Vijayanagara Empire, derives its lineage from Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a formidable warlord hailing from the Tulu-speaking region in the west.
 
• His son, Narasimha Nayaka, orchestrated the downfall of the feeble Narasimha Raya II, thus ending the reign of the Saluva dynasty.
 
• Subsequently, Narasimha Nayaka ascended to the Vijayanagara throne as Viranarasimha Raya, marking the ascendancy of the Tuluva dynasty.

questions.question: In diffraction of white light by a prism, which colour of light from VIBGYOR will be bent most?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When white light travels through a prism, **violet light** bends the most, while red light bends the least.
 
• This occurs because violet light possesses the shortest wavelength among the seven colors in white light, while red light has the longest.
 
• **The dispersion of light,** which separates white light into its constituent colors, is responsible for this phenomenon.
 
• The refractive index of the medium is highest for violet light and lowest for red light. Refraction occurs as light enters the prism at an angle, with the degree of deviation varying based on wavelength. Consequently, different colors deviate at distinct angles, resulting in their separation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Violet light**, with the shortest wavelength among the seven constituent colors of light, experiences the greatest deviation, while red light, with the longest wavelength, undergoes the least. 
 
• Thus, the order of colors, commonly remembered as **VIBGYOR (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red),** reflects this sequence based on their respective wavelengths and degrees of deviation.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• **The basic circular flow model of the economy **operates without government intervention.
 
• This model illustrates the interconnected flow of money, goods, and services among economic participants.
 
• It serves as the foundation for national accounting and macroeconomics.
 
• Additional details about the **circular flow model** include:
 
 
• It delineates the overall structure of the economy, depicting exchanges between households and firms through both the factor and product markets.
 
• Households contribute land, labor, and capital to firms.
 
• Households purchase goods and services from firms in the product market.
 
• Firms compensate households for the resources they supply, which constitute factors of production.
 
• In reality, the model becomes more intricate with the inclusion of two additional elements: government involvement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Various circular flow models exist, each tracking a different number of sectors. 
 
• The following sectors could be incorporated into a circular flow model. Typically, each sector is denoted by a capital letter, often associated with GDP calculation methods. 
 
• Governments determine their gross national income by monitoring all injections into and withdrawals from the circular flow of income. When leaks match injections, the circular flow of income for a nation is deemed balanced.

questions.question: The Physical Quality of Life Index does NOT include which of the following indicators?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender development index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index** does NOT include Gender development index.
 
• **The Gender Development Index (GDI) **is a metric crafted to assess gender equality. 
 
• It, along with the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM), was introduced in the 1995 Human Development Report by the United Nations Development Program. 
 
• These measures were devised to imbue the Human Development Index (HDI) with a gender-sensitive perspective. The GDI was the initial outcome of this effort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) **seeks to gauge a country's well-being by averaging three equally weighted statistics: basic literacy rate at age 15, infant mortality, and life expectancy at age one.
 
• Developed in the mid-1970s by M.D. Morris for the Overseas Development Council, emerged from dissatisfaction with using Gross National Product (GNP) alone as a development indicator.
 
• Morris aimed to capture various aspects of development, including health, education, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• While PQLI offers an improvement, it faces challenges inherent in quantifying quality of life. Critics point out the overlap between infant mortality and life expectancy as a limitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The level of physical quality **of life is often seen as indicative of a country's economic development.
 
• A country with a higher physical quality of life is typically considered more developed than one with a lower quality.
 
• This assessment is based on three key standards: the extent of education, life expectancy, and infant mortality rate.

questions.question: What numerical scale was introduced in 1932 that determined the electronegativity of fluorine to be 4.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pauling scale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity,** a concept pioneered by **Linus Pauling in 1932,** measures an atom's ability within a molecule to attract electrons towards itself. It's described as "the power of an atom in a molecule to attract electrons to itself."
 
• On the Pauling scale, fluorine is set as the benchmark with an electronegativity of 3.98, and other elements are gauged relative to this value.
 
• Essentially, an atom's electronegativity indicates its tendency to pull electron density towards itself when forming bonds.
 
• Higher electronegativity signifies a stronger pull on electrons during bonding.
 
• Atomic number and atomic radius largely influence an atom's electronegativity.
 
• Across the periodic table, electronegativity generally increases from left to right and from bottom to top.
 
• Consequently, fluorine stands as the most electronegative element, while francium exhibits the least electronegativity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Allred-Rochow Electronegativity **method quantifies the electrostatic force resulting from the effective nuclear charge acting on the valence electrons of an atom.
 
• Mulliken's scale of electronegativity defines electronegativity as an inherent characteristic of an element, solely contingent on the valence state of the atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity** is the measure of an atom's ability to attract shared electrons in a covalent bond. A higher electronegativity value indicates a stronger attraction for the shared electrons. 
 
• This property follows a predictable trend across the periodic table: electronegativity generally increases from bottom to top within groups and from left to right across periods. 
 
• Consequently, fluorine holds the title of the most electronegative element, whereas francium ranks among the least electronegative.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution?

questions.question: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in a Water Cycle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The hydration** step is NOT involved in a Water Cycle.
 
• **Hydration** involves replenishing the **body fluids** that are lost through sweating, exhaling, and waste elimination.
 
• Typically, the body loses and requires to replacement of approximately 2-3 quarts of water each day.
 
• Fortunately, many of the foods we consume are predominantly made up of water. Examples of such foods include leafy greens, as well as most fruits and vegetables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The water cycle,** also referred to as the hydrologic cycle or hydrological cycle, illustrates the perpetual movement of water across the Earth's surface, in the atmosphere, and beneath it.
 
• Throughout this cycle, water undergoes transitions between different states, while the total quantity of water particles remains constant.
 
• These state changes encompass processes such as evaporation, melting, freezing, sublimation, condensation, and deposition, all of which necessitate the input or release of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation** represents the transformation of water vapor in the atmosphere into liquid water, contrasting with the process of evaporation. This step is pivotal in the water cycle as it leads to the formation of clouds.
 
• Above 0 degrees Celsius, water vapor condenses into water droplets. However, this condensation doesn't occur spontaneously; it relies on the presence of dust or other impurities. Water vapor adheres to the surface of these particles, eventually forming droplets. As these droplets coalesce, they precipitate out of clouds and onto the ground below, a phenomenon known as **precipitation or rainfall**.
 
• The sun serves as the primary energy source, driving much of the evaporation observed on Earth. **Evaporation** typically occurs when water molecules on the surface of bodies of water become energized and ascend into the atmosphere.

questions.solution:
Given:

Two circles touch each other internally.

The radius of the inner circle = 3 cm

**Concept used:**

When two circles are touch each other internally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png]

Then, 

Radius of inner circle (PD) = x cm

Radius of bigger circle (OB) = y cm

OP = Distance between two centers = Radius of bigger circle - radius of inner circle

⇒OP = y - x

CD = Diameter of inner circle = 2 × (radius of inner circle)

⇒ CD = 2x

OC = Difference between chord and bigger circle centre = CD - PD - OP

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 2x - x - (y - x) = 2x - y

Calculation:

Let the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle = AB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png]

PD = 3 cm 

OD = 4 cm

OP = OD - PD

⇒ OP = 4 - 3 = 1 cm

⇒ CD = 2 x PD = 2 x 3 = 6 cm

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 6 - 3 - 1 = 2 cm

⇒ OB = 4 cm = radius of outer circle

By using Pythagoras theorem, we can write that

OB2 = BC2 + OC2

⇒ 42 = BC2 + 22

⇒ BC2 = 16 - 4

⇒ BC2 = 12

⇒ BC = sqrt{12} = 2sqrt{3} cm

Now, 

The length of biggest chord AB = 2 x BC = 2 x 2sqrt{3} = 4sqrt{3} cm

**∴ The length of the biggest chord of the circle outside the inner circle is 4sqrt{3} cm.**

In the opposite direction,

then Relative speed = (x + y) km/hr

Distance = speed x time

They are moving in the same direction,

Relative speed = (54 - 36) km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 km/hr

Distance = Speed x time
